notes: Both jobs were driven against the same live contracts by the same scheduler key.
The provider is a real staked node (tier 1, 20 tOMC bond) registered on chain.
Image bytes never touch the chain; only keccak256 digests do.

No worker process was alive during either run. The node was heartbeated once (node-worker.js --once) so it stays eligible, then left with nothing behind it. That is deliberate: the failure path needs a provider that never delivers, and a live worker would race the harness for the same job. The picker's allowOffline override is therefore in force and says so in both logs.

The provider side of both jobs is the harness's own stub, not a second process. The separate claim that a node process can live behind this address is evidenced by its heartbeat transactions, which are real on-chain writes.
Inference ran with --no-infer: the delivered artefact is a deterministic stub. The digest binding, the escrow, the fee and the slash are unaffected.
